title: Bob Carroll's street fight and his drinking
summary: Caldwell recalls pulling Bob Carroll off a fight on Seventh Avenue; he drank enough to raise hell but was no alcoholic.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, but he -- didn't he die. Wasn't he getting to be an alcoholic?

Yeah, he drank, and one day wewere out there on 132nd Street by the Rhythm Club, and there's a bar on the corner. So we go out there talking, and I went to the bar. We worked downstairs there. So Bob, he said, Happy, he said, come on out and get straight (unintelligible) and buy a bottle. I said, Bob, we'll get in trouble, said, what Bob? Bob Carroll. So I went out there with Bob (unintelligible) had him by the heck. guy anybody make. They were wrestling around all over Seventh Avenue.
I said, hey, Bob, said, get up before the police come and lock you guys, lock you up. Bob said, I got this son of a bitch down, Hap, and I'm going to whip him up good.
I said, Bob, come on. Get up. I said, here come the policeman. I'm going to hold him (unintelligible). I'm going to whip him. I said, oh, no, this guy going to get put in jail.
He died -- they told me that, of course, Bob would drink, but he never was what you call a
alcoholic, but he just would drink enough to act foolish, raise hell.
He wasn't evil. He was just -- yeah.

No, just that way. (Unintelligible) saw the crowd, so the policeman come, and I said, Bob, if you don't get up from there, the man going to take you to your come on (unintelligible) now. Where's the (unintelligible)? I said, there up on 133rd Street. I'm going to whip this sucker again. I said, oh, man, said, would you come on? This is Happy talking to you. All right, Hap. Jumped up, kicked the came in all dirty Come on to the bar, guy. (unintelligible), man, come on. Bob (unintelligible). I said, get a drink right quick.
Did you find out what they were fighting about?
Nobody knew. I don't know what Bob -- Bob -- could have been something -- he would -- Bob would get full of that whiskey, he'd chew the policeman.
But I mean he -- I was trying to think whether it was with Don Redman's records. He sounded very good.
That was -- I loved his playing.
